summary: Our project tells the story of the equipment NASA has left on the Moon and Mars, like the Apollo lunar rover, the Spirit and Opportunity rovers, and the Voyager probes. We made a simple presentation for school students that explains what each machine was built for, what it discovered, and what happened to it in the end. We wanted to show that these old machines are not really forgotten, because the science they did still helps new missions today
details: Our project tells the story of equipment NASA has left behind on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space, written for school students. What it does: We made a 7-slide presentation that introduces each machine in simple words. It covers the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle and Surveyor landers on the Moon, the Spirit, Opportunity and Ingenuity on Mars, and the Voyager probes in deep space. For each one we explain what it was built for, what it discovered, and how its mission ended. How it works: We collected facts and real photos from NASA's public mission pages and image library, then organised them into a short story that students can follow quickly. We used Gamma to build the slides and kept the text short and easy to read. Benefits: Students learn about space history and the science behind these missions in a few minutes, without needing any background. Intended impact: We want students to see that old space hardware is not forgotten, because the science it did still helps plan new missions. Tools used: Gamma (presentation), NASA Image and Video Library (photos), NASA mission websites (facts).
